items.pdf_text:
CENTRAL ELECTRICITY REGULATORY COMMISSION
NEW DELHI
No. L-1/261/2021/CERC Dated: 11.11.2026
NOTIFICATION
In exercise of the powers conferred by sub-section (1) of Section 178 and clause
(ze) of sub-section (2) of Section 178 read with clause (47) of Section 2, clause
(d) of sub-section (2) of Section 38, clause (c) of Section 40 and clause (c) of sub-
section (1) of Section 79 of the Electricity Act, 2003 and all other powers
enabling it in this behalf and after previous publication, the Central Electricity
Regulatory Commission hereby makes the following regulations to amend the
Central Electricity Regulatory Commission (Connectivity and General Network
Access to the inter-State Transmission System) Regulations, 2022 (hereinafter
referred to as “the Principal Regulations”) namely:
1. Short Title and Commencement
1.1. These regulations may be called the Central Electricity Regulatory
Commission (Connectivity and General Network Access to the inter-State
Transmission System) (Fourth Amendment) Regulations, 2026 or ‘fourth
amendment regulations’.
1.2. These regulations shall come into force with effect from the date of their
publication in the Official Gazette.
2. New Definition in Regulation 2.1
2.1. A new clause, namely, clause (b-i) shall be inserted after clause (b) in
Regulation 2.1 of the Principal Regulations, as under:
“(b-i) "Authority" shall have the same meaning as defined in sub-
section 6 of Section 2 of the Act;”
2.2. Four new clauses, namely, clause (w-i), clause (w-ii), clause (w-iii) and
clause (w-iv) shall be inserted after clause (w) in Regulation 2.1 of the
Principal Regulations, as under:
“(w-i) “Land BG” means Bank Guarantee furnished under clause (vii)(c)
or clause (xi)(c) of Regulation 5.8 of these regulations;
(w-ii) “Land BG route” means route covered under clause (xi)(c) of
Regulation 5.8 of these regulations;
Central Electricity Regulatory Commission (Connectivity and General Network Access to
1
the inter-State transmission System) (Fourth Amendment) Regulations, 2026

(w-iii) “Land route” means route covered under clause (xi)(b) of
Regulation 5.8 of these regulations;
(w-iv) “LoA route” or “PPA route” means route covered under clause
(xi)(a) of Regulation 5.8 of these regulations;”
3. New Regulation 3.10
3.1. A new Regulation, namely, Regulation 3.10, shall be added after
Regulation 3.9 of the Principal Regulations, as under:
“3.10 Notwithstanding anything contained in Regulations 3.7 to 3.9
of these Regulations, an entity shall be eligible to seek
withdrawal of full Connectivity quantum (no partial withdrawal
shall be permitted), subject to the following:
(a) For cases where final grant of Connectivity has been issued
and the time period is two years or more;
(i) between the date of intimation of in-principle grant of
Connectivity and the date of intimation of the final grant
of Connectivity; or
(ii) between ‘likely start date of connectivity’ intimated in in-
principle grant of Connectivity and start date of
Connectivity intimated in final grant of Connectivity
(tentative or firm);
And
the request for withdrawal is made to the Nodal Agency within
a period of 45 days from intimation of final grant of Connectivity.
(b) For cases where final grant of Connectivity has not been
issued even after lapse of two years from the date of intimation
of in-principle grant of Connectivity, such entity may also seek
withdrawal of full quantum of Connectivity under this
Regulation, within a period of 45 days from lapse of two years
from intimation of in-principle grant of Connectivity.
(c) The withdrawal shall be processed by the Nodal Agency
within a period of 15 days from the date of the withdrawal
application, with intimation to the Applicant.
(d) In case the withdrawal application is accepted by the Nodal
Agency, all BGs (Conn-BGs and Land BG, as applicable) shall
be returned.
(e) Application fee shall be forfeited on withdrawal of the
Connectivity.”
4. Amendment to Regulation 4.1 of the Principal Regulations:
Central Electricity Regulatory Commission (Connectivity and General Network Access to
2
the inter-State transmission System) (Fourth Amendment) Regulations, 2026

4.1. The words “, with a minimum energy capacity (in MWh) as twice the
Power capacity (in MW) or as notified by the Authority as per system
requirement.” shall be added at the end of clause (c) of Regulation 4.1 of
the Principal Regulations.
5. Amendment to Regulation 4.2 of the Principal Regulations:
5.1. The words “and Regulation 5.11 of these regulations” shall be inserted
after the words “Regulation 4.1” in Regulation 4.2 of the Principal
Regulations.
6. New Regulations 4.7 and 4.8
6.1. New Regulations, namely, Regulation 4.7 and Regulation 4.8, shall be
added after Regulation 4.6 of the Principal Regulations, as under:
“4.7 An REGS or ESS with an installed capacity of 50 MW and above
individually or with an aggregate installed capacity of 50 MW and
above through a Lead Generator or a Lead ESS, as the case may be,
may seek Connectivity for non-solar hour access at substations other
than those covered under Regulation 4.5(a) of these regulations. The
application shall be processed as per clause 2A of Annexure-IV of
these regulations. CTUIL shall publish a list of such substations
along with the margin available for non-solar hours access and shall
update the same on a monthly basis.
4.8 An application for grant of Connectivity with full day access under
Regulation 4.1 of these regulations, may be converted to an
application for ‘solar hours access’ or ‘non-solar hours access’ under
these regulations based on the availability of margin declared during
the consultation meeting. In such cases, once the applicant
furnishes its written consent, the Nodal Agency shall process such
application in terms of the applicable provisions for grant of
Connectivity with solar hour access or non-solar hour access, as the
case may be. The vice versa shall also be applicable.”
7. Amendment to Regulation 5.1 of the Principal Regulations:
7.1. A new proviso shall be added after the second proviso to Regulation 5.1
of the Principal Regulations, as under:
“Provided also that the capacity for meeting technical compliances at
the Point of Injection (POI) (as confirmed by the Nodal Agency after
studies) shall not be counted under installed capacity for the purpose
of seeking Connectivity at ISTS.”
8. Amendment to Regulation 5.2 of the Principal Regulations:
8.1. The words “(along with application fees of Rs. 5 lakh for the capacity
50MW and above, and Rs. 1 lakh for the capacity less than 50MW, with
Central Electricity Regulatory Commission (Connectivity and General Network Access to
3
the inter-State transmission System) (Fourth Amendment) Regulations, 2026

applicable taxes)” shall be inserted after the words “shall make an
application” in clause (a) of Regulation 5.2 of the Principal Regulations.
8.2. The words “(in case of Land BG, it may be furnished by the existing
Connectivity grantee or the entity installing the additional capacity)”
shall be added at the end of clause (h) of Regulation 5.2 of the Principal
Regulations.
8.3. Four new clauses, namely, clause (l), clause (m), clause (n) and clause
(o), shall be added after clause (k) under Regulation 5.2 of the Principal
Regulations, as under:
“(l) In case additional capacity is an ESS, such ESS may install
REGS for the purpose of charging such ESS only. The installed
capacity of such REGS shall be indicated in the application and
the requirement of documents under Regulation 5.8 or
Regulation 11A for Land or Financial Closure shall not be
applicable for such REGS.
(m) In case the existing Connectivity Grantee relinquishes the
Connectivity or its Connectivity is revoked, for the full quantum
of Connectivity, the connectivity of capacity under Regulation 5.2
of these regulations shall also stand relinquished or revoked.
However, if the existing Connectivity grantee relinquishes a
part quantum of Connectivity or its partial Connectivity is
revoked, the Connectivity of capacity under Regulation 5.2 of
these regulations shall be restricted to the balance Connectivity
quantum and the remaining quantum, if any, shall be revoked.
(n) In case additional capacity is for meeting technical compliance
clauses (e), (g), (h), (i) of this Regulation shall not be applicable
for such capacity.
(o) In case the additional capacity which is not covered under clause
(n) of this Regulation and which does not result in additional
solar hour access or non-solar hour access, clauses (e), (h) and
(i) of this Regulation shall not be applicable for such capacity:
Provided that clause (i) shall be applicable to the extent of
achieving the CoD of such additional capacity in terms of
Regulation 24 of these regulations.”
9. Amendment to Regulation 5.6 of the Principal Regulations:
9.1. The words “[application under Regulation 4.1(e)]” in the main paragraph
of Regulation 5.6 of the Principal Regulations shall be deleted.
10. Amendment to Regulation 5.8 of the Principal Regulations:
Central Electricity Regulatory Commission (Connectivity and General Network Access to
4
the inter-State transmission System) (Fourth Amendment) Regulations, 2026

10.1. The words “or sub-lease documents (where lease permits sub-lease),”
shall be inserted after the words “land use rights”, and the following
proviso shall be added after the first proviso, in sub-clause (b) of clause
(vii) of Regulation 5.8 of the Principal Regulations:
“Provided further that such sub-lease documents shall be
permitted only (i) between Parent and subsidiary(ies) and vice
versa or between subsidiary(ies) of the same Parent or (ii) in the
case where leased Government land is sub-leased to other entity
under Government policy.”
10.2. Proviso (ii) and (iii) to clause (xi)(a) of Regulation 5.8 of the Principal
Regulations shall be substituted as under:
“(ii) In case of the Applicant being multi-located REGS, where single
LOA or PPA provides for establishment of projects at multiple
locations, the applicant shall be eligible to obtain Connectivity
based on such LoA or PPA, at one or more locations, upto the
quantum for which LoA has been awarded or PPA has been
executed or Installed capacity provided in the LOA or PPA at such
location, whichever is lower. In case Connectivity is sought using
part quantum of LOA or PPA and part quantum of Land or Land
BG at any of the locations (under sub-clause (iii) of this Proviso),
the quantum of LOA or PPA to be used at such location shall be
exhausted first upto the Connectivity quantum, before the
balance quantum of LoA or PPA, if any, can be utilised for another
location. For the balance capacity, if any, at any such location
where the balance quantum of LOA or PPA falls short of the
installed capacity at such location and for capacity at other
locations provided in the LOA or PPA, the applicant shall be
eligible to seek the additional Connectivity under Regulation
5.8(xi)(b) or Regulation 5.8(xi)(c) of these regulations.
Note: Multi-located REGS shall mean REGS located in one or
more States, and connected at different substations.

(iii) For an Applicant covered under sub-clauses (i) and (ii) of this
clause, where LOA or PPA quantum is less than Installed capacity
mentioned in the LoA at the location at which Connectivity has
been sought based on such LoA and the entity wishes to seek
Connectivity for a quantum more than LOA or PPA quantum at
such location, it may apply through a single application with LOA
or PPA for part quantum and with documents based on clause (b)
or clause (c) of Regulation 5.8(xi) of these regulations for the
balance quantum of Connectivity for such location. The Nodal
Agency shall process the grant of such Connectivity at such
location, treating the full quantum of Connectivity sought as a
single generating station, where SCOD for such generating
station shall be considered based on LOA or PPA at such location.
The compliance of the land documents under Regulation 11A of
these regulations shall be met for the quantum of Connectivity
covered under clauses (b) or (c) of Regulation 5.8(xi). The SCOD
for such a generating station at any such location, for the
purpose of Regulation 24.6(1)(a) of these regulations shall be that
of LOA or PPA.”
10.3. The words “or sub-lease documents (where lease permits sub-lease),”
shall be inserted after the words “land use rights”, and the following
proviso shall be added after the first proviso in sub-clause (b) of clause
(xi) of Regulation 5.8 of the Principal Regulations:
“Provided further that such sub-lease documents shall be
permitted only (i) between Parent and subsidiary(ies) and vice
versa or subsidiary(ies) of the same Parent or (ii) in the case where
leased Government land is sub-leased to other entity under
Government policy.”
Central Electricity Regulatory Commission (Connectivity and General Network Access to
6
the inter-State transmission System) (Fourth Amendment) Regulations, 2026

10.4. A new proviso shall be added to clause (xi)(c) of Regulation 5.8 of the
Principal Regulations, as under:
“Provided that in case the Applicant is an ESS (excluding Pumped
Storage Plant (PSP)), the Bank Guarantee shall be Rs. 5 lakh/MW.”
10.5. The words “or Renewable Power Park Developer,” shall be inserted after
the words “ESS (excluding Pumped Storage Plant (PSP))” in the main
paragraph of clause (xii) of Regulation 5.8 of the Principal Regulations.
11. Amendment to Regulation 5.10 of the Principal Regulations:
11.1. A proviso shall be added in clause (f) of regulation 5.10 of the Principal
Regulations, as under:
“Provided that a second change of land parcels shall be permitted
in terms of Regulation 9.3.5 of these regulations.”
12. Amendment to Regulation 5.11 of the Principal Regulations:
12.1. The words “(400MWh)” shall be inserted after the words “ESS- 200MW”
in Example, and following proviso shall be added under clause (c) of
Regulation 5.11 of the Principal Regulations:
“Provided that ESS with such REGS shall have minimum energy
capacity (in MWh) as twice of its Power capacity (in MW) or as notified
by the Authority as per system requirement, failing which such
REGS shall not have injection scheduling rights under GNA for ESS
during non-solar hours.”
13. Amendment to Regulation 6.3 of the Principal Regulations:
13.1. Regulation 6.3 of the Principal Regulations shall be substituted as
under:
“6.3 The Nodal Agency shall close the application(s) and return all the
Bank Guarantees furnished, if any, along with full application fee
in the following conditions:
(a) Nodal Agency is unable to carry out the interconnection
study to identify the requirement of augmentation to the
existing ISTS, if any, on account of Load Generation Balance
or other associated issues for enabling transfer of power over
ISTS under General Network Access.
(b) The identified augmentation (with or without ATS) is not
approved by the authority competent to approve such
augmentation.
Central Electricity Regulatory Commission (Connectivity and General Network Access to
7
the inter-State transmission System) (Fourth Amendment) Regulations, 2026

(c) The closure of the application shall be in accordance with
the Detailed Procedure to be formulated by the Nodal Agency
in consultation with the relevant stakeholders.”
14. Amendment to Regulation 7.2 of the Principal Regulations:
14.1. The words “, or within 30 days from the approval of the identified
augmentation by the authority competent to approve such
augmentation, whichever is later” shall be added at the end of the main
paragraph of Regulation 7.2 of the Principal Regulations.
15. Amendment to Regulation 9.3 of the Principal Regulations:
15.1. The words “or 18 months prior to the firm start date of Connectivity”
shall be substituted with the words “6 months prior to the firm start date
of Connectivity” in sub Regulation 9.3.1 of Regulation 9.3 of the Principal
Regulations.
15.2. The following provisos shall be added under sub Regulation 9.3.5 of
Regulation 9.3 of the Principal Regulations, as under:
“Provided that a second source change shall be permitted with a fee
of Rs 20,000/MW (for the gross change of capacity of source) or Rs.
10 lakhs per application, whichever is higher:
Provided further that in case the second source change requires
change of land parcel and one change of land parcel (as permitted in
terms of Regulation 5.10) is already exhausted, the second change in
land parcels shall be permitted with a combined fee of Rs. 25,000/MW
(for the gross change of capacity of source) or Rs. 10 lakhs per
application, whichever is higher:
Provided also that the applicable fee shall be intimated by the Nodal
Agency along with the permission for source change, which shall be
furnished by the entity within fifteen (15) days of the date of such
intimation, failing which permission for change of source shall stand
revoked.
Illustration: Suppose an entity has been granted Connectivity for
400 MW under clause (xi)(a) of Regulation 5.8 and has the Installed
capacity as 300 MW: Solar, 300 MW: Wind.
Suppose the entity seeks a first source change as 400 MW: Solar,
200MW: Wind and 50MW: ESS. After the first source change, the
entity shall have connectivity of 400MW with injection scheduling
right for 400MW in solar hours and for 250MW during non-solar
hours (considering 200 MW Wind and 50 MW ESS).

Case-1: Suppose the second change of source is sought as: Installed
Capacity: 500 MW Solar, 100 MW Wind and ESS 100 MW. In such
case the, gross change in source is 200 MW (|400-500| + |200-100|
= 200 MW) and, the applicable fee shall be Rs 40 lakhs (200 X Rs
20000) for such change. In case solar hour access shall be 400 MW
and non- solar access shall be 200 MW, considering addition of 50
MW ESS
Case-2 : Where both, i.e., land parcels change and source change,
are required-
In the above example, the applicable fee shall be Rs 50 lakhs (200 X
Rs 25000) for such a change.
Note: Approval of land parcel changes and source change shall be
processed in terms of Regulation 5.10 and Regulation 9.3,
respectively.”
16. Amendment to Regulations 11A of the Principal Regulations:
16.1. The words “in-principle grant of Connectivity or” shall be inserted before
the words “final grant of connectivity has been intimated at an ISTS
substation” in the first proviso to clause (1) of Regulation 11A of the
Principal Regulations.
16.2. A new Clause, namely, clause (1A) shall be inserted after Clause (1) of
Regulation 11A of the Principal Regulations, as under:
“(1A) A Connectivity Grantee which is REGS (other than Hydro
generating station) or ESS (excluding PSP) covered under clause
(xi)(a) of Regulation 5.8 shall submit documents for land in terms
of sub-clause (b) of clause (xi) of Regulation 5.8 of these
regulations, within 60 days of the effective date of GNA, if not
furnished already in terms of sub-clause (iv) of clause (xi)(a) of
Regulation 5.8 of these regulations.”
16.3. Clause (2) of Regulation 11A of the Principal Regulations shall be
substituted as under:
“(2) A Connectivity Grantee which is REGS (other than Hydro
generating station), ESS (excluding PSP) or Renewable power
park developer shall furnish the financial closure documents
(copy of loan sanction letter or proof of first disbursal of loan
amount or copy of Board resolution, if internal funding is planned
for 100% of the project cost, along with net worth and other
details as per the Detailed Procedure to be issued by the Nodal
Agency) for the capacity of such Connectivity, within 30 days of
the effective date of GNA:
Central Electricity Regulatory Commission (Connectivity and General Network Access to
9
the inter-State transmission System) (Fourth Amendment) Regulations, 2026

Provided that if the entity has already achieved the CoD of the full
capacity as on the last date of furnishing financial closure
documents in terms of this Clause, such entity shall not be
required to furnish the financial closure documents.”
16.4. The main paragraph of clause (4) of Regulation 11A of the Principal
Regulations shall be substituted as under:
“(4) An entity, which has applied for Connectivity under clause (xi)(b)
or clause (xi)(c) of Regulation 5.8 and has been issued in-principle
or final grant of Connectivity, furnishes a PPA, as eligible under
clause (xi)(a) of Regulation 5.8, (entered into by itself or its
subsidiary company or its Parent company or any other subsidiary
of the Parent company of such entity, as the case may be), either
for part capacity or full capacity, may apply to the Nodal Agency
for conversion of its Connectivity under clause (xi)(b) or clause
(xi)(c) of Regulation 5.8 to clause (xi)(a) of Regulation 5.8, subject
to the following:”
16.5. The words “LOA or” in the main paragraph of sub-clause (a) of clause (4)
of Regulation 11A of the Principal Regulations shall be deleted.
16.6. A new sub-clause (v) shall be added after sub-clause (iv) under clause
(4)(c) of Regulation 11A of the Principal Regulations, as under:
“(v) If Connectivity quantum remaining under Land route or Land BG
route after conversion to PPA route is less than 50 MW, such
remaining quantum shall be treated as relinquished with return
of Conn-BG3 and Land BG, if any, for such relinquished quantum
and Conn-BG1 and Conn-BG2, as applicable, shall be retained
against the converted quantum of Connectivity.”
16.7. Two new sub-clauses, namely, sub-clause (h) and sub-clause (i) shall be
inserted after sub-clause (g) under clause (4) of Regulation 11A of the
Principal Regulations, as under:
“(h) The conversion from Land route or Land BG route, to PPA route,
shall be in accordance with the provisions of clause (xi)(a) of
Regulation 5.8 including the provisions under clauses (i) to (iii) of
the proviso to clause (xi)(a) of Regulation 5.8 of these regulations.
(i) An entity may seek conversion of route of multiple applications
under Land BG route or Land route (including enhancement
application) as an application under PPA route, where such
multiple applications have been granted at the same terminal bay
or same substation. Such conversion shall be in terms of clause (ii)
of Proviso to clause (xi)(a) of Regulation 5.8 and clause (4) of
Regulation 11A of these regulations.”
Central Electricity Regulatory Commission (Connectivity and General Network Access to
10
the inter-State transmission System) (Fourth Amendment) Regulations, 2026

16.8. Clause (5) of Regulation 11A of the Principal Regulations shall be
substituted as under:
“(5) The conditions subsequent to the intimation of in-principle grant
of Connectivity or final grant of Connectivity, required to be
completed under Regulation 11A and achieving COD shall be
met, either by the entity to which the in-principle or final grant of
Connectivity is issued, or by its Parent company or its subsidiary
company(ies) or by any other subsidiary company(ies) of the
Parent company of such entity, as the case may be. All the
responsibilities under these regulations shall continue to be with
the entity to which in-principle or final grant of Connectivity is
issued, including submission of documents inter-alia for PPA or
Land or Financial closure as applicable. The documents required
to be submitted to the Nodal Agency shall include an
authorisation issued by the entity in whose name the documents
of PPA or Land or Financial Closure or COD are furnished,
enabling the entity which is issued in-principle or final grant of
Connectivity to furnish the same to the Nodal Agency.”
16.9. Following words shall be inserted after the words “Clause (1) of
Regulation 11A of these regulations,” in Clause (1) of Regulation 11B of
the Principal Regulations:
“or an entity covered under clause (xi(a)) of Regulation 5.8, fails to
submit the documents in accordance with clause (1A) of Regulation
11A of these regulations,”
17. Amendment to Regulations 15.1 of the Principal Regulations:
17.1. The words “and 15.3” shall be substituted with the words “to 15.5” in
the main paragraph of Regulation 15.1 of the Principal Regulations.
18. Amendment to Regulations 15.3 of the Principal Regulations:
18.1. The words “implementing the REGS (whose documents were furnished
by the Connectivity Grantee for meeting compliance of Financial Closure
and COD under Regulation 11A(5) of these regulations)” shall be
substituted with the words “achieving the CoD” in the main paragraph
of Regulation 15.3 of the Principal Regulations.
19. New Regulations 15.4 and 15.5
19.1. Two new Regulations, namely, Regulation 15.4 and Regulation 15.5
shall be added after Regulation 15.3 of the Principal Regulations, as
under:
Central Electricity Regulatory Commission (Connectivity and General Network Access to
11
the inter-State transmission System) (Fourth Amendment) Regulations, 2026

“15.4 The Regulations 15.1 to 15.3 of these regulations shall be
subject to the permitted change in control under clause (6) of
Regulation 11A of these regulations.
15.5 If the generating station or ESS which has achieved COD is
transferred to or acquired by another entity, the Connectivity for
such generating station or ESS which has achieved COD shall
also be transferred to the entity to whom the generating station
or ESS has been transferred to or acquired by. In case Conn-BGs
are subsisting, the generating station or ESS may substitute
Conn-BGs in the name of the entity to whom such generating
station or ESS has been transferred to or acquired by. The Nodal
Agency shall carry out consequential changes in the Connectivity
Agreement to incorporate such transfer.”
20. Amendment to Regulations 16.2 of the Principal Regulations:
20.1. The words “in five equal parts over five years corresponding to the
generation” shall be substituted with the words “within one week after
expiry of one year from the declaration of COD of the corresponding” in
Regulation 16.2 of the Principal Regulations.
21. Amendment to Regulation 17.1 of the Principal Regulations:
21.1. Clause (iv) under Regulation 17.1 of the Principal Regulations shall be
deleted.
22. New Regulation 17.5 of the Principal Regulations:
22.1. A new Regulation, namely, Regulation 17.5, shall be added after
Regulation 17.4 of the Principal Regulations, as under:
“17.5 Dual Connection for drawee entities: to the ISTS and intra-
state transmission system or distribution system
(1) A drawee entity having connectivity to an intra-State
transmission system or distribution system may seek to
connect to ISTS directly as an applicant under Regulation
17.1(iii), for part quantum (not less than 50MW) or full
quantum of the drawal capacity for which it is already having
Connectivity to an intra-state transmission system or
distribution system along with consent of the concerned STU
and Distribution Licensee, as applicable, clearly specifying the
quantum of Connectivity to STU or Distribution system, as the
case may be. Such an entity shall continue to pay the
applicable charges under the Act and regulations framed
therein for both the connections. Such applicable charges may
include Cross Subsidy Surcharge (CSS), additional surcharge,
transmission charges, wheeling charges, standby charges, or
Central Electricity Regulatory Commission (Connectivity and General Network Access to
12
the inter-State transmission System) (Fourth Amendment) Regulations, 2026

any other charges approved by the Appropriate Commission.
The concerned STU and Distribution Licensee may process the
application for consent in a time-bound manner such that
open access is facilitated.
(2) A GNA grantee covered under Regulation 17.1(iii) of these
regulations may get connected to the intra-state transmission
system or the distribution system for part quantum or full
quantum of GNA granted under Regulation 17.1(iii) of these
regulations, in terms of the concerned State Regulations, after
obtaining consent of the Nodal Agency that such a connection
is technically feasible and subject to payment of applicable
charges under the Act and regulations framed therein for both
the connections. Such entity shall confirm the quantum of
Connectivity to STU or the Distribution system, as the case
may be, to the nodal agency.
(3) The provisions under clauses (1) and (2) of this Regulation shall
not be applicable to entities having GNA unless GNA is
RE RE
converted to GNA.”
23. Amendment to Regulation 20.2 of the Principal Regulations:
23.1. Regulation 20.2 of the Principal Regulations shall be deleted.
24. Amendment to Regulation 22.2 of the Principal Regulations:
24.1. The words “Regulation 16” shall be substituted with the words
“Regulations 16.1 to 16.4” in clause (b-ii) of Regulation 22.2 of the
Principal Regulations.
24.2. Clause (c) of Regulation 22.2 of the Principal Regulations shall be
deleted.
24.3. Main paragraph of clause (d) of Regulation 22.2 of the Principal
Regulations shall be substituted as under:
“(d) Entities covered under Regulation 4.1 and clause (iii) of Regulation
17.1 of these regulations shall furnish one-time GNA charge of Rs. One
lakh per MW for the quantum of GNA within 15 days of the effective
date of the GNA. In case such charges are not furnished by the entity
within the specified timeline, the same shall be recovered by
encashment of Conn-BG1, Conn-BG2 and Conn-BG3 as required. In
case no Conn-BGs are subsisting, and the entity does not furnish the
required charges, such entity shall not be eligible for carrying out any
transactions with the Grid till the charges are furnished by the entity.

granted GNA under clauses (ii) to (v) of Regulation 17.1 of

load (specified in the GNA grant), where such load is

be transferred to such new entity owning the load, subject

granted GNA under clause (vi) of Regulation 17.1 of these
regulations, and where such generating station or ESS is
transferred to or acquired by another entity. The GNA shall
be transferred to such new entity owning the generating
